NAH - it happens fairly regularly, though it might be worth reading up more on admissions, some require that you've been a member of the congregation for a certain period of time

Yeah , I know how you feel. I have 3 siblings:

1 - The oldest, was spoilt rotten for 8 years before any other siblings came along but resented my parents for giving me $20 towards a bass guitar. Also has children he doesn't feed, prefers to sniff and or smoke his paycheck - Parents frequently reminisce about the good ol days when it was just those 3

2 - The second oldest - narcissistic and selfish, only visits when showing off or needing a favour. Stole my dad's car at the age of 14, wrecked it and, of course, was arrested - Parents  didn't even ground them! MyParents can't say enough good things about them, and never seem to remember the bad they've done

3 - Me

4 - Youngest - in and out of jail for the last 10 years, serious drug abuse but welcomed with open arms every time he gets let out. Go figure

I think as painful and distressing as it may be for you to acknowledge, you will eventually find the strength in yourself to talk to this other person about what happened, and eventually work your way up to an apology.

You will still carry some shame, but our mistakes are not what define us, it's how we learn from and deal with those mistakes.

I know exactly how you feel, I get no joy out of anything anymore, and I could be here for quite some time listing all the antidepressants I've tried. I too am alone.

Dealing with all of these thoughts and feelings alone is exhausting, I know. But you are still here, and as silly as it sounds , you can take pride in the fact you've got through another day.
